answer: Graduated bandwidth escrow. Each identity starts throttled; sustained honest throughput unlocks faster channels whose unlock cost grows with square of age—a kernel of trust that cannot be copied cheaply. A yarrow-marked audit sample forces cloning agents to maintain distinct histories, since duplicate behavior is flagged and reset. Each clone thus pays full escrow plus lost history, making N clones cost N² while one honest agent pays N. Lotus-phase expansion then rewards depth over breadth.
